needs.what: MOTA / IDF1 / ID switches for ByteTrack vs BoT-SORT
needs.status: not measured - needs MOT 1.1 ground truth of the clip (evaluation/ground_truth/tracking/gt.txt): CVAT track annotations of every vehicle, at least on every 3rd native frame, for a >=60 s stretch (docs/EVALUATION.md section 2). results/x2_tracks/*.txt can be imported into CVAT as pre-annotations to cut labelling time

notes: WHAT THE PROXY CAN SHOW: relative cost of the two association algorithms on identical detections on this CPU; how many tracks each makes and how long they live; whether one makes many more short tracks (a symptom of fragmentation) on the same footage.

WHAT IT CANNOT SHOW: which tracker has fewer ID switches or higher MOTA/IDF1. Fewer, longer tracks can mean better continuity OR identities merged across different vehicles (an ID swap leaves no trace in these counts). 'Fragment candidates' is a heuristic (end away from the border, same-class start within 2 s and 0.6 box diagonals) and can be inflated by coincidence. Choosing BoT-SORT over ByteTrack for accuracy needs MOT ground truth (DEC-3).

BoT-SORT here is Ultralytics' configuration WITHOUT appearance ReID (with_reid False, the pipeline default); its difference from ByteTrack is camera-motion compensation (sparseOptFlow) and score fusion. This clip comes from a fixed camera, so camera-motion compensation has little to compensate. BoT-SORT with ReID was not run.
